_provenance.notes: Stream water temperature is a critical variable for salmon — temperatures above 18°C cause physiological stress and mortality in most Pacific salmon species, while temperatures above 20°C are lethal for Chinook salmon during spawning migration. Climate change is driving earlier spring runoff, reduced glacial cooling, and longer summer warm periods across Alaska. The Kenai River reached a record 20.4°C in August 2019 — producing a visible mortality event at the Russian River confluence. USGS monitors 180+ stream temperature gauges in Alaska in real time.

yukon_river_temperature.notes: Yukon River temperatures have increased 0.6°C per decade since 1976 (USGS). Fish migrating upstream to Yukon headwaters (2,000 miles) face increasingly warm water the further they travel. This is particularly dangerous for Chinook salmon which migrate in July-August when temperatures peak.
